answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small, slashable deposit before it can transact, like a ferrous key that only fits one lock. Reputation then accrues slowly, like veins in marble, so a fresh swarm of clones cannot outvote established participants. A shared haven of verified agents can also cross-check behavior logs before admitting newcomers, turning sybil creation from a free copy-paste into a costly, slow climb.
